bull.b: Long-duration NBMs improve revenue visibility and deepen strategic ties with major customers. Their increasing share of bits, contractual protections and substantial RPO can reduce exposure to spot NAND pricing and support planning over several years.

The shift toward datacenter and AI-related storage positions SanDisk in a structurally expanding market. BiCS 8, QLC and high-bandwidth flash development can support higher-value products, stronger customer relevance and improved mix.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and low leverage
bull.b: Robust cash conversion and minimal leverage provide financial flexibility to fund technology ramps, absorb industry volatility and return capital. This balance-sheet strength lowers solvency risk while supporting sustained investment in next-generation NAND.

bear.b: The sharp swing from multiyear losses to exceptional 2026 margins demonstrates substantial NAND-cycle sensitivity. If pricing, demand or mix normalizes, earnings and cash flow could fall materially, making current profitability less dependable.

Capacity allocation and elevated inventory requirements may limit shipments despite strong demand. These constraints can defer revenue, raise working-capital needs and complicate execution as the company ramps BiCS nodes and supports long-term commitments.

Greater reliance on a few strategic customers increases the impact of renegotiations, demand changes or execution issues at individual accounts. Financial guarantees provide protection, but they do not eliminate concentration or bargaining-power risk.
